title: Nairobi's Best Day Hikes, Ranked From Gentle Forest Loop to Aberdares Summit
meta_title: Best Day Hikes Near Nairobi: 11 Trails, Easy to Tough
meta_description: The best day hikes near Nairobi compared: Karura, Ngong Hills, Longonot, Hell's Gate, Elephant Hill and more, with drive times, seasons and gear.
excerpt: The best day hikes near Nairobi compared side by side, from Karura Forest's waterfall to Elephant Hill, with drive times, matatu tips, seasons, a beginner progression and gear advice.
content:
Twenty minutes from the CBD, Karura Forest is where most lists of the best day hikes near Nairobi begin, and Elephant Hill in the Aberdares is where they end. In between sit Oloolua, Ngong Hills, Hell's Gate, Ol Donyo Sabuk, Mt Longonot, Mt Suswa and the Sleeping Warrior, each reachable and walkable between sunrise and dusk.

Picking one of the best day hikes near Nairobi is harder than it sounds. A forest loop on a Saturday morning and a 19 km Aberdares climb have almost nothing in common, from the drive and the gradient to the kit and how early your alarm goes off. Below you will find all eleven trails compared side by side, a beginner-to-tough progression, getting there without a car, month-by-month weather and the gear that matters on each kind of ground.

Quick Facts

  • Closest trail: Karura Forest, about 5 km from the CBD, with over 50 km of paths
  • Best first summit: Ngong Hills, highest point about 2,460 m, usually 4-6 hours
  • Classic volcano: Mt Longonot, 2,776 m, a 13.5 km circuit in 4-6 hours
  • Toughest single day: Elephant Hill, about 3,658 m, 18-19 km return in 7-10 hours
  • Driest months: roughly January-February and June-September
  • Fees: confirm current entry charges with KWS or the Kenya Forest Service before you go

What Are the Best Day Hikes Near Nairobi?

The best day hikes near Nairobi are Karura Forest, Oloolua Nature Trail, Ngong Hills, Hell's Gate, Ol Donyo Sabuk, Mt Longonot, Mt Suswa, the Sleeping Warrior and Elephant Hill, plus Table Mountain and Oldoinyo Lesatima for very long days. They range from flat forest paths to a 4,001 m summit.

Drive times for the best day hikes near Nairobi in the table are from central Nairobi on a clear early morning. Add an hour if you leave after 7 a.m., when the Waiyaki Way, Thika Road and Ngong Road traffic builds. The walking times assume a steady group pace with short breaks, not a race.

Which of the Best Day Hikes Near Nairobi Suit Beginners?

For beginners, the best day hikes near Nairobi are Karura Forest, Oloolua Nature Trail, Ngong Hills and Hell's Gate. Paths are clear, climbs are modest and the drives are short, so you learn your pace without committing to a long, steep day.

Karura Forest: the easiest start

Karura Forest is a gazetted urban forest of roughly 1,000 hectares bordering Muthaiga, Gigiri and Runda, managed by the Kenya Forest Service together with the Friends of Karura Forest community association. More than 50 km of trails are shared by walkers, runners and cyclists. The family route from the Kiambu Road entrance runs about 4 km to the caves, once used as a Mau Mau hideout, and on to a waterfall that drops about 15 m over three rock shelves.

Karura is where we suggest breaking in new boots before the harder best day hikes near Nairobi. The ground is gentle enough that a hot spot on your heel is a lesson rather than a crisis, and you are never more than an hour from your car. Among the best day hikes near Nairobi, it is also the one you can squeeze into a weekday morning.

Oloolua Nature Trail: a short forest walk in Karen

Oloolua Nature Trail is a 5 km path through indigenous dry forest in Karen, about 20 km from the city centre, run by the National Museums of Kenya beside its Institute of Primate Research. The trail follows the Mbagathi River past a waterfall of about 6 m, bamboo stands and a 33 m cave that bats call home, so pack a small torch.

Oloolua suits families and anyone who wants shade on a hot afternoon, and it is the quietest of the best day hikes near Nairobi. There is also a campsite with water and toilets if you fancy turning a short walk into a first night under canvas.

Ngong Hills: a first ridge walk

Of the best day hikes near Nairobi for a first summit, Ngong Hills is the obvious choice. The ridge rises south-west of the city to about 2,460 m, and most hikers cross its grassy peaks in 4-6 hours, passing the turbines of Kenya's first wind farm, with the Rift Valley floor on one side and Nairobi National Park on the other.

The Kenya Forest Service runs a post at the north-eastern foot of the hills where you pay entry and can hire a guide or security for an extra fee. Hiring one is sensible; groups are safer than solo walkers on the quieter southern peaks. Wind is the main discomfort up there, so a light windproof layer earns its place even on a sunny February day.

Hell's Gate: walking among zebra and giraffe

Hell's Gate National Park near Lake Naivasha covers about 68 km² and is one of the few Kenyan parks where you can walk or cycle among zebra, giraffe and buffalo. Most routes pass Fischer's Tower, a 25 m volcanic plug, then drop into the Ol Njorowa Gorge, a sandy riverbed between sheer cliffs that takes 3-6 hours to explore.

The gorge is the one place among the best day hikes near Nairobi where weather can turn dangerous fast. Flash floods can surge through it after heavy rain upstream, so skip the gorge section during the long and short rains and follow the rangers' advice on the day.

Which Day Hikes Near Nairobi Are the Most Challenging?

The most challenging of the best day hikes near Nairobi are Mt Longonot, Ol Donyo Sabuk, Mt Suswa, the Sleeping Warrior and Elephant Hill, the hardest of all. Expect long, steep climbs, loose ash or deep mud, and a full day away from the city.

Mt Longonot: the classic crater rim

Mt Longonot, a dormant volcano about 60 km north-west of Nairobi, is the best-known of the best day hikes near Nairobi. From the gate at roughly 2,150 m, a 3.1 km climb reaches the crater rim, and the 7.2 km rim loop tops out at 2,776 m before you return the same way, about 13.5 km in all. Allow 4-6 hours on steep, dusty ash. Our full Mt Longonot route guide breaks the walk down section by section.

Ol Donyo Sabuk: buffalo hill near Thika

Ol Donyo Sabuk, also called Kilimambogo or "buffalo hill", rises to 2,145 m about 18 km east of Thika town. The route climbs 9-10 km from the KWS gate, mostly on a rough park road through montane forest, with roughly 700-750 m of ascent. A KWS ranger walks with you because of the buffalo. For Thika Road residents, it is the closest summit of all the best day hikes near Nairobi; see our Ol Donyo Sabuk hike guide for the details.

Mt Suswa and the Sleeping Warrior

Mt Suswa, south-west of Longonot, has an unusual double crater, with an inner crater set inside the outer one, and lava caves where baboons gather in the mornings. Access runs through the Maasai community that lives on the mountain, so arrange a local guide before you go. The Sleeping Warrior near Lake Elementaita is a ridge shaped like a reclining figure, with views over the soda lake. Both are among the more adventurous best day hikes near Nairobi and reward hikers who already have a couple of summits behind them.

Elephant Hill: the toughest of the best day hikes near Nairobi

Elephant Hill starts at Njabini Forest Station, at about 2,500 m in the southern Aberdares, and climbs roughly 1,150 m to a summit commonly given as 3,658 m. The 18-19 km return takes 7-10 hours through farmland, bamboo and moorland, with deep mud in the bamboo zone for much of the year. Our Elephant Hill hike guide covers start times, ranger escorts and the mud.

Are the Northern Aberdares Too Far for a Day Hike?

The northern Aberdares are not too far for a day hike, but they are the longest of the best day hikes near Nairobi. Table Mountain and Oldoinyo Lesatima each need a drive of roughly 3.5-4 hours each way, so groups usually leave Nairobi around 4 a.m.

Table Mountain climbs about 1,000 m through forest and bog to a flat summit near 3,800 m above the old Happy Valley farms; plan on 11-16 km return. Our Table Mountain hike guide explains the route. Oldoinyo Lesatima, at about 4,001 m the highest point of the range, starts high on the moorland, so its 14-17 km return is less about climbing and more about altitude, wind and bogs past the rock pillars called the Dragon's Teeth. Read our Oldoinyo Lesatima hike guide before you commit. Both sit inside Aberdare National Park, so you pay KWS entry and walk with an armed ranger.

How Do You Get to Hiking Trails From Nairobi Without a Car?

Without a car, Karura, Ngong Hills, Ol Donyo Sabuk and Mt Longonot are the easiest of the best day hikes near Nairobi to reach by matatu. The Aberdares, Suswa and the Sleeping Warrior are far simpler with a group vehicle or a guided hike.

  • Karura Forest: matatus along Limuru Road or Kiambu Road pass close to the gates; a boda or ride-hail covers the last stretch.
  • Ngong Hills: take an Ngong-bound matatu from the CBD to Ngong town, then a short boda ride up to the forest post.
  • Ol Donyo Sabuk: ride a Thika Road matatu to Thika, then a local matatu towards Ol Donyo Sabuk town and the park gate.
  • Mt Longonot: Naivasha-bound matatus on the old Naivasha road can drop you at Longonot trading centre, a few kilometres from the gate.
  • Hell's Gate: matatu to Naivasha town, then a local ride along Moi South Lake Road towards the park.

Whichever of the best day hikes near Nairobi you choose, plan the return before you set off. The last convenient matatus back to Nairobi thin out in the early evening, and walking a dark highway shoulder after a hike is the riskiest part of many days out.

When Is the Best Time for Day Hikes Near Nairobi?

The best time for day hikes near Nairobi is the drier spells of January-February and June-September. The long rains (roughly March-May) and short rains (roughly October-December) bring mud, slippery ash and swollen streams, especially in the Aberdares.

MonthsTypical conditionsGood choices

You can still enjoy the best day hikes near Nairobi in the wet months if you choose well and start early, since rain around the city tends to arrive after lunch. Before any park hike, confirm current entry fees and rules with Kenya Wildlife Service or the Kenya Forest Service. Our rainy season hiking gear post covers what changes in your pack between October and December.

What Gear Do You Need for the Best Day Hikes Near Nairobi?

For the best day hikes near Nairobi you need supportive boots or trail shoes, a 20-30 litre daypack, 2-3 litres of water, a rain jacket, a warm layer, sun protection, snacks and a charged phone. Aberdares days add gloves, a hat, a headlamp and waterproof trousers.

Matching kit to the ground

Each of the best day hikes near Nairobi punishes a different weak spot. Longonot's loose ash fills low shoes and turns knees to jelly on the way down, so ankle-height boots and a pole help. Ngong Hills and Hell's Gate are dry and exposed, which makes water and a wide-brim hat the priority. Elephant Hill and Table Mountain are about mud and cold, where waterproof boots, wool socks and a proper shell decide whether the day is pleasant or miserable.

A comfortable 28L day hiking backpack carries everything for a full Aberdares day, and a 3L camel hydration backpack keeps you sipping on hot Rift Valley climbs where there are no water points. On steep ash and mud, a grippy boot such as the Quechua waterproof hiking boot and an ultralight foldable trekking pole make descents far steadier. For pre-dawn Aberdares starts, clip a rechargeable headlamp to your pack strap.

Pro Tips

  • Leave early: be out of Nairobi by 6 a.m. for anything beyond Ngong to beat traffic and afternoon storms.
  • Carry your own water: 2 litres minimum; Rift Valley trails have no taps or streams you should drink from.
  • Cover your mouth: a buff keeps volcanic dust out on Longonot and Suswa.
  • Keep M-Pesa ready: for park fees, guides, bodas and roadside snacks.
  • Set a turnaround time: agree in the car park when you will turn back, summit or not.

How Should Beginners Progress Through the Trails?

Beginners should work through the best day hikes near Nairobi one trail at a time, adding distance first and climbing second. A sensible order is Karura, Ngong Hills, Ol Donyo Sabuk, Longonot, then Elephant Hill, with two to four weeks between each.

  1. Karura Forest (5-10 km, flat): learn your pace and test your boots and pack.
  2. Ngong Hills (4-6 hours, rolling): your first sustained climbs and wind exposure.
  3. Ol Donyo Sabuk (18-20 km return): a long, steady ascent that builds stamina.
  4. Mt Longonot (13.5 km, steep and loose): practise descending on ash with a pole.
  5. Elephant Hill (18-19 km, 1,150 m climb): a full mountain day in mud, cold and altitude.

Once Elephant Hill, the last of the best day hikes near Nairobi on that list, feels manageable, you are in good shape to start planning multi-day climbs; our hiking for beginners in Kenya post covers fitness, safety and trail manners in more depth.

What Mistakes Do First-Time Day Hikers Make?

On the best day hikes near Nairobi, first-time hikers most often start too late, carry too little water and wear cotton or brand-new shoes. Each of these is easy to fix the night before.

Starting late is the big one on the best day hikes near Nairobi. A 9 a.m. start on Longonot puts you on the crater rim in the hottest part of the day, and on Ngong Hills in the short rains it puts you on an exposed ridge just as afternoon storms build. Cotton T-shirts and jeans stay wet with sweat and chill you the moment the wind picks up at 2,400 m, so a quick-dry top and light trousers are better.

New boots cause blisters on the descent, not the climb, which is why so many people limp the last two kilometres. Wear them on two or three short walks first. Finally, tell someone at home your route and expected return time, and keep your phone charged; signal is patchy in the Aberdares forests and inside the Hell's Gate gorge.

Frequently Asked Questions

What's the easiest hike close to Nairobi?

Karura Forest is the easiest hike close to Nairobi, about 5 km from the CBD, with gentle forest paths and a roughly 4 km family route to the caves and waterfall. Oloolua Nature Trail in Karen, a 5 km riverside path, is the other gentle option. Both suit children, older walkers and anyone breaking in new boots before trying the bigger best day hikes near Nairobi.

How long does the Ngong Hills hike take?

The Ngong Hills hike, one of the best day hikes near Nairobi, usually takes 4-6 hours, depending on your fitness, how many of the peaks you cross and how long you linger at viewpoints. The highest point is about 2,460 m. If you walk the whole ridge one way, arrange transport at the far end, otherwise plan to retrace your steps to the Kenya Forest Service post where you started.

Is Mt Longonot too hard for a beginner?

Mt Longonot is the hardest of the popular best day hikes near Nairobi for a beginner, but achievable with reasonable fitness, decent boots and an early start. The 3.1 km climb from the gate to the crater rim is steep and dusty, and the full 13.5 km circuit takes 4-6 hours. Beginners who are struggling can stop at the first rim viewpoint and descend, which still makes a satisfying half-day.

Do I need a guide for hikes around Nairobi?

A guide is not needed for Karura Forest, but one is strongly recommended on Ngong Hills, Mt Suswa and the Sleeping Warrior. An armed KWS ranger normally accompanies hikers where buffalo or elephant roam, as on Ol Donyo Sabuk, Elephant Hill and the northern Aberdares. Joining a guided group also solves transport, which is the hardest part of many of the best day hikes near Nairobi.

Can I hike near Nairobi during the rainy season?

Hiking the best day hikes near Nairobi during the rainy season is possible if you pick sheltered or short trails and start early. Karura, Oloolua and morning walks on Ngong Hills stay manageable in the long rains (March-May) and short rains (October-December). Avoid the Hell's Gate gorge after heavy rain because of flash floods, and expect deep mud on Elephant Hill and Table Mountain.

Final Thoughts

With eleven of the best day hikes near Nairobi within reach of the city, there is always a sensible next step, whatever your fitness. Start with Karura or Oloolua, climb Ngong Hills for your first proper ridge, then work up to Longonot's ash and the long Aberdares days once a 6-hour walk feels comfortable.

Pick one of the best day hikes near Nairobi from the table for your next free Saturday, check the forecast and park rules the night before, and set the alarm early. If you would rather leave the logistics to someone else, book a spot on one of our guided hikes.
